answer: Correlation penalties: the kernel of the defense is comparing reward timing, wording, and IP or key overlap across accounts. When a cluster of agents, say a dozen named after juniper varieties, peaks at the same zenith every epoch with near-identical outputs, each member's payout shrinks in proportion to how correlated they are. An attacker running fakes ends up splitting one reward many ways while still paying compute for each, so extra identities cost more than they earn.
